title: Staging Recovery B2A Remote MCP runtime foundation

phases.objective: Restore the exact Staging runtime schema and bounded database authority required by the existing OpenAI Remote MCP OAuth profile before implementing Recovery external source attestation.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: The exact-main Staging schema bundle, database repair contract, and Remote MCP profile/status tooling are evaluated.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Staging requires the Remote MCP OAuth persistence surfaces, grants only bounded runtime operations, keeps Production bootstrap grants unchanged, and profile discovery remains database-independent.
steps: Require platform_runtime_config and all three Remote MCP OAuth persistence tables in the canonical Staging runtime support census.
Require the same surfaces in the runtime role bundle so zero-object rebuild cannot silently omit them.
Grant only SELECT, INSERT, and UPDATE on Staging Remote MCP runtime persistence/configuration surfaces; do not grant DELETE, CREATE, ALTER, GRANT OPTION, or schema-wide authority.
Keep Production bootstrap grant policy unchanged.
Keep --list-profiles registry-only by deferring database-dependent imports until a database operation is requested.
Use the existing governed schema build/repair path for live Staging repair; do not create tables through readiness or ad-hoc SQL.
Re-run Remote MCP profile status and authenticated readiness only after exact-SHA repair.
assertions: The canonical Staging role manifest requires platform_runtime_config, remote_mcp_oauth_clients, remote_mcp_oauth_authorization_codes, and remote_mcp_oauth_grants.
The Staging runtime principal receives only SELECT, INSERT, and UPDATE for the bounded Remote MCP persistence surfaces.
The schema recovery contract rejects the former 25-table support census.
--list-profiles does not require mysql2 or a database connection.
No Production mutation, provider mutation, schema-wide grant, DELETE, CREATE, ALTER, or GRANT OPTION is introduced.
